question: A black hole as a river of space

scene.title: A black hole as a river of space
scene.subtitle: Space flows inward, faster closer in. Light swims through it at light speed. The horizon is where the flow wins.
scene.takeaway: A black hole’s horizon is where space flows inward at light speed. Inside, even light is carried in.

beats.title: Still space
beats.body: Without a black hole, space is still. A flash of light swims outward at light speed and gets away.

beats.title: Space starts to flow
beats.body: Add a black hole and space flows inward, faster closer in. Light always swims at light speed through the flowing space. Out here the flow is slower than light, so the flash still escapes, slowly.

beats.title: Past the horizon
beats.body: At the horizon the flow equals light speed: an outward flash stands still. Inside, the flow is faster than light and sweeps every flash inward.

scene.why: It explains a black hole’s edge, the event horizon, without equations: the place where space flows inward as fast as light can swim.
scene.opening: Light always moves at light speed. So why can’t it escape from inside a black hole?

questions.q: Just outside the horizon, can a flash sent outward escape?
questions.a: Yes, slowly: the inflow there is a little slower than light.

questions.q: What happens to a flash sent outward exactly at the horizon?
questions.a: It stays where it is: the inflow equals light speed.

questions.q: If the black hole were heavier, would its horizon be bigger or smaller?
questions.a: Bigger: the place where the inflow reaches light speed is farther out.
